newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight orders emerge, Yemen features.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight orders emerge, Yemen features.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a mixed bag of quoted origins on Tuesday as a number of new orders emerged for various destinations.
Yemen proved popular as a buyer, with Louis Dreyfus quoting two new orders for bagged sugar.

It was open for 12,000 tonnes from Thailand and a further 12,000 from east coast Mexico, both for prompt shipment. Dreyfus also fixed a prompt 12,000-tonne bagged cargo to Yemen from Puerto Quetzal. The rate was unknown.
Other new business came from E D & F Man, which quoted for 7,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Foynes to Nigeria for prompt dates and 3,000 tonnes in bags from Corinto to Chile.
Nissho Iwai was open for 16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Japan for prompt/onwards shipment dates.
Shipbrokers said Benham or nominee fixed 14/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Punta Morales to Toronto for April 15/25. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.
Benham was also reported to be on subjects with a bulk parcel of 6,200 tonnes from the Dominican port of San Pedro de Macoris to US Gulf/Atlantic.
